stories: A regional European retail bank had accumulated 30 different account offerings over time. The large number of choices made it harder for the sales force to sell them and customers didn't know which was best. After interviewing customers and identifying three segments (Comfort, Direct, Classic), the bank created three new offerings. Sales skyrocketed after the reduction because each product became distinct and salespeople could articulate each product's value.
summary: Product configuration and bundling are critical design decisions when monetizing innovation. Configuration involves selecting which features and functionalities to include in a product for each customer segment based on their needs, value perception, and willingness to pay. Successful configuration requires designing products with only the features customers will pay for, establishing clear distinctions between offerings to prevent cannibalization, and having the discipline to exclude features even when tempted to add value.
